html:
The Ngalakgan are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, on the Roper River in southern Arnhem Land. The map shows them as Ngalakan from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Mangarayi to the west, the Ngandi and Ngalkbun to the north and east and the Alawa to the south. In 1908 the Anglican church founded the Roper River mission, now Ngukurr, which gathered people from many groups after years of violence from cattlemen. Children there grew up speaking a new creole language, Kriol, which spread across the north and is now spoken by thousands. Ngalakgan itself has almost no speakers left.
